title: Chapter Practice: Chemical Reactions & Equations MCQs
objectives: Evaluate student mastery of balanced equations, redox identification, and corrosion prevention

blocks.heading: Practice Instructions
blocks.content: Analyze chemical equations for stoichiometry, oxidation numbers, and displacement rules.

practice.prompt:
Which of the following statements about the reaction below are INCORRECT?
2PbO(s) + C(s) -> 2Pb(s) + CO2(g)
(i) Lead is getting reduced.
(ii) Carbon dioxide is getting oxidised.
(iii) Carbon is getting oxidised.
(iv) Lead oxide is getting reduced.
hints: Statements (i) and (ii) refer to products (Lead, CO2). Oxidation and reduction occur on REACTANTS!
Lead oxide (PbO) is reduced to Pb; Carbon (C) is oxidised to CO2.
practice.feedback: PbO is reduced (not lead), and Carbon is oxidised (not carbon dioxide). Therefore statements (i) and (ii) are incorrect.

practice.prompt: A shiny brown coloured element 'X' on heating in air becomes black in colour. Name the element 'X' and the black coloured compound formed:
hints: Copper is shiny reddish brown. When heated in oxygen, it forms black copper(II) oxide.

practice.prompt: Which gas is flushed into potato chip packets to prevent rancidity?
hints: An unreactive inert gas is used to prevent oxidation of oils and fats.
practice.feedback: Nitrogen is an inert antioxidant gas that displaces oxygen and prevents oxidative rancidity of fats.

takeaways: Always check whether oxidation/reduction statements describe reactants or products.
Copper oxide (CuO) is black; copper metal is reddish brown.
